questions.q: What do successful people focus on most, according to Tracy?
a: What they want and how they will get it
What could go wrong and who to blame
How they compare with their competitors
How much time they have left each day
questions.why: Lesson 1 says successful people put their attention on their goals and how to reach them.

questions.q: Which of these does the summary list as a principle of effective goals?
a: They should be specific, measurable and time-bound
They should be ambitious but open-ended
They should be shared with everyone you know
They should be chosen by someone you trust
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists six principles, starting with specific, measurable and time-bound goals.

questions.q: What does Tracy mean by goals being in harmony?
a: Your goals should not work against each other
Your goals should match your partner's goals
Your goals should all share one deadline
Your goals should sound positive when spoken
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns that conflicting goals, like a marathon and a startup, will make both fail.

questions.q: Why does Tracy say making goals realistic matters?
a: Small wins strengthen your belief that you can succeed
Realistic goals need less planning and effort
Realistic goals impress other people more
Realistic goals can be reached without deadlines
questions.why: Lesson 3 says achieving realistic goals more often confirms your belief in yourself.

questions.q: Why does Tracy ask you to list reasons your goal would improve your life?
a: More reasons make you want the goal more
It helps you predict problems in advance
It shows others that the goal is sensible
It replaces the need for a deadline
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the more reasons you find, the stronger your desire to reach the goal.
